item.title: Denmark spared space debris: Europe might be hit
item.description: Chinese space debris, currently at nearly 140 kilometers altitude, might impact Europe, though not Denmark. Astrophysicist Mads Skakke Fredslund from Aarhus University explained that the debris is a booster rocket used by China, now falling towards Earth. item.title: Denmark breaks Euro curse, taking down Germany
item.description: Led by the tournament MVP, Mathias Gidsel, the Danish men’s handball team will be honoured at Copenhagen City Hall on Monday afternoon. The Danish men’s handball team now holds the Olympic, World, and European titles, a feat previously achieved only by France. The triumph was secured when Denmark defeated Germany 34-27 in the European Championship […]

item.title: Veterans protested US president’s failure
item.description: Several thousand people participated in a protest march from Kastellet to the U.S. Embassy in Copenhagen, expressing dissatisfaction with U.S. President Donald Trump’s remarks about NATO soldiers in Afghanistan. Danish veterans found Trump’s comments derogatory, undermining Denmark’s mission, which cost 44 soldiers their lives. item.title: Denmark sends 100M kr to children in need worldwide
item.description: During this year’s Danmarks Indsamling, 100,513,291 kroner were collected. This marks an increase from last year’s 86 million kroner. The funds are directed towards humanitarian efforts for children in need in areas including Somalia, Sudan, Uganda, and Afghanistan. item.title: Fewer stores in Denmark, but more employees
item.description: Over the past decade, the number of stores in Denmark has decreased by about ten percent, from 25,632 in 2014 to 23,088 in 2024. However, the number of retail jobs has increased by eight percent, reaching 264,882.
